toolCallDetails.arguments: {"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_openai-gpt-6.1-sol_01.html","edit_description":"Create the complete self-contained HTML deliverable, with embedded CSS and JS only, no libraries/assets/WebGL. Build an elegant dark full-window Canvas 2D demo with cyan/blue cube, small title 'GOURAUD / SOFTWARE RENDERER', FPS readout, and accessible clickable Wireframe (W) and Pause (P) buttons plus keyboard shortcuts (ignore repeats). requestAnimationFrame loop and resize handling. Implement genuine software triangle rasterization in bounded-resolution offscreen Canvas ImageData (cap logical raster size around 800x600 while preserving viewport aspect), composite via main Canvas 2D drawImage. Eight cube vertices ±1, explicitly outward-wound six quad faces with per-face colors; rotation using explicit X/Y/Z rotation matrices applied to vertices and face normals. Camera at origin viewing positive z, cube translated z=5.5, perspective x=cx+f*x/z and y=cy-f*y/z. Cull using dot(camera-space outward normal, face camera-space position)<0 for visible faces. Split each visible quad into two triangles. Compute per-face per-corner Lambert lighting from moving point light to rotated vertex, using rotated flat face normal, ambient + diffuse and mild distance falloff so corners have distinct intensities; no per-pixel lighting. Barycentric rasterization over clipped pixel bounding boxes, robust winding-independent weights, reciprocal depth buffer and perspective-correct interpolated RGB (interpolate color/z and 1/z), write RGBA to ImageData. Clear image each frame transparent and depth Infinity. Draw tasteful background/grid/vignette on main 2D canvas then raster image. Moving light visible as small glowing projected marker with label (keep depth in safe range). Wireframe overlay only visible culled faces with triangle edges including diagonal, mapped correctly from raster to canvas; toggle overlays while keeping shading. Pause freezes simulation time for cube and light but keeps rendering FPS accurate, initial delta clamped to avoid jumps. FPS updated from frame timestamps over ~500 ms; status reflects running/paused. Include clear concise code comments explaining matrices, culling, Lambert per-vertex, perspective interpolation and barycentric rasterization. Ensure outward windings correct: vertices 0(-1,-1,-1),1(1,-1,-1),2(1,1,-1),3(-1,1,-1),4(-1,-1,1),5(1,-1,1),6(1,1,1),7(-1,1,1); faces front near [0,3,2,1], far [4,5,6,7], left [0,4,7,3], right [1,2,6,5], bottom [0,1,5,4], top [3,7,6,2]. Canvas responsive on mobile. Deliver polished working complete file."}
